verdictReason: The only claimed edge is price ($15 vs $40), which is not structural. Topic-level agenda alerts already exist free or near-free across the same cities (Voterheads: free for 5 orgs, $2.50/org beyond, 1,500+ cities; Legistar native keyword alerts), the data layer is a commodity, and verified payers are professionals at $200-800/month sold by phone/association, not $15 hosts reachable cold. Cash-positive on paper but ~$1/hour of owner time.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Three verified in this pass. (a) Legistar's own alerts: a user can create an alert that emails when search terms are added to the Agenda Items page, so a host in a Legistar city can watch 'short-term rental' for free per city (no fee mentioned on the guide page). (b) Voterheads: topic-level tracking of council meetings, free for up to five organizations, $2.50/month per organization beyond that, active in 1,500+ cities and counties in 41 states. (c) An Apify Legistar actor with a title keywordFilter, billed per city queried (about $5.50 per 1,000 city queries per the page), for the DIY route. Not re-verified by me (pages could not be fetched): City Watch free tier, Locunity free tier, AgendaWire $40 watchlist with an STR example (old ids MED-02-E1/E3/E4/E5). What the free tools do NOT do: a pre-built STR bundle, so the entrant's only difference is skipping a few minutes of per-city setup (board-level city notifications, e.g. Louisville, are not topic-aware, which is the one gap).

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None. The scan-1 edge is cash_cost only (shared pipeline lets a $15 price). Cheaper/automation/niche focus is not an edge under the brief, and the pipeline is copyable in days: the Legistar data layer is a commodity (D7), and Voterheads/Topic Watch already run user-defined topic engines across many councils (D3, D5); AgendaWire's own homepage already demos an STR watchlist (E4, unverified by me). A vertical preset is a configuration of an existing engine. A defensible edge would need an exclusive or compounding asset (e.g. a verified STR-ordinance outcome database nobody else has) and none is part of the idea. Falsifier of this verdict: documented STR hosts, solar installers or liquor licensees paying >= $15/month for agenda alerts with no free tool in their city.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Professionals and organizations, at much higher prices and through sales-led channels: Agenda Discovery (Colorado Politics, 2017) was 'available now for $200 to $800 a month, depending on the number of users' (originally reported for 2016); OrdinanceWatch sells to law firms ('Designed for lawyers as a client retention tool') and associations with pricing by phone; Topic Watch (UK) lists GBP 250 and GBP 450 per month for unlimited councils; Stateside sells analyst-curated 'concierge' monitoring. At the low end Voterheads is free up to 5 orgs and $2.50/org. I found no evidence that individual STR hosts, solar installers or liquor-license holders pay $15/month for agenda alerts. The paying segment (lawyers, associations, lobbyists) is reached via relationships, which the stranger rule excludes.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Agendas and ordinances are public records, so reading them is low legal risk, but the entrant depends on each city's portal: the Apify actor page itself warns 'Not every city runs Legistar'; PDF-only and PrimeGov towns need fragile scraping (maintenance cost uncosted). I could not read the Legistar Web API terms or PrimeGov API terms (fetch refused on provenance), so API rate limits, per-client access rules and any redistribution limits are unverified. Summaries must link to source documents and must not be presented as legal advice (rules are jurisdiction-specific; OrdinanceWatch positions itself for lawyers). Email sending needs CAN-SPAM-compliant unsubscribe and a physical address (general knowledge, not sourced here).

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers?
answers.answer: Reference entrant per case file: $400 startup, 45 days to first revenue, 12 h/week. Base case (all inputs assumptions except the $15 price from the case file): paying subscribers ramp linearly +5/month to 60 at month 12 = 390 subscriber-months x $15 = $5,850 revenue; cost = $400 startup + $40/month hosting and summarization x 12 + $50 domain + payment fees (2.9% + $0.30) = about $1,217; profit about $4,633. Pessimistic (price x0.8 = $12, volume x0.5 = 195 subscriber-months, cost x1.5): revenue $2,340, cost about $1,585, profit about $755, so technically positive. But the base volume (60 paying subscribers at $15 against free/$2.50 alternatives and no audience) is unsupported by any evidence; 12 h/week x 52 = 624 h at $755 is about $1.2/hour; and the model excludes scraping upkeep. Cash-positive is not the problem; the problem is that the price is above the free tier of the alternatives.

killReasons.reason: Topic-level agenda alerts already exist free or near-free in the same cities (Voterheads: free for 5 orgs, $2.50/org beyond, 1,500+ cities/41 states; Legistar native search-term alerts; DIY Apify actor at cents). The entrant's $15 price sits above these, and its only difference is a pre-built STR bundle that saves a few minutes of setup.

No structural edge: the scan-1 edge is price only, powered by a commodity data layer (Legistar actor, D7) and a topic engine that rivals already run (Voterheads D3, Topic Watch D5, AgendaWire STR watchlist E4); a vertical preset is a config change any incumbent can ship, so the entrant has nothing exclusive or compounding.

Verified payers are professionals and associations at $200-$800/month or by phone quote (Agenda Discovery, OrdinanceWatch, Topic Watch, Stateside); no evidence that individual STR hosts, solar installers or liquor licensees pay $15/month, and the professional segment is reached through relationships, which the stranger rule excludes.
OrdinanceWatch already sells Short Term Rentals as one of 128 issue categories in Florida, so a vertical STR alert exists at least regionally; the wedge is not novel there.

assumptions: Price $15 per topic bundle per month: taken from the case file (itself an estimate, not a sourced willingness to pay).

ASSUMPTION costs: $400 startup (case file) + $40/month hosting and LLM summaries x 12 + $50 domain/misc + payment fees 2.9% + $0.30 per charge (about $287 base) = about $1,217; scraping upkeep for PDF-only towns not costed in cash, absorbed in owner hours.
Pessimistic: price x0.8 = $12; volume x0.5 = 195 subscriber-months => revenue $2,340; non-fee fixed costs $930 + fees $126 = $1,056, x1.5 = about $1,585; profit about $755.
Owner time: 12 h/week x 52 = 624 h, so pessimistic return is about $1.2 per hour; owner labour is not in cost365.
Churn and refunds ignored (would lower revenue).
